canal_p18_001.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_001.text: The forty-second morning began with the later rota spread across the keeper's bench. Its columns looked beautiful: day, receiving duty, person, contact and replacement. Luo had asked for a useful schedule, and the clerk had made one clean enough to frighten Yue. At the margin, old household headings supplied several convenient contacts. Tian tapped her own family's former entry, which now sat beside a winter preparation call she had never accepted. The clerk said it only helped him remember the street. Tian asked why the street seemed to have acquired her hours.

canal_p18_002.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_002.text: He crossed out the unaccepted call at once. The old heading stayed only where it identified an actual address, with no work availability carried from it. Yue suggested asking current receivers to read their own proposed rows before the sheet was posted. The clerk disliked losing his neat morning to interviews. Luo gave him tea and said she disliked replacing another failed gate more. Tian took the cup away from the paper edge before either of them made the argument wet.

canal_p18_003.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_003.text: The young keeper confirmed his two short winter morning rounds under the quoted monthly keeper allowance. Luo retained the remaining accepted rounds and oversight within that same four-copper keeper line. Their intervals were receiving tasks at agreed fixed terms, not whole repair days hired at the earlier daily rate. Extra weather work would require its actual authorization and costs before borrowing another person. The young man marked his shop deliveries beside the rounds. One collided with market morning, and he asked to shift that particular check earlier.

canal_p18_004.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_004.text: Luo wanted the check at the old familiar hour. He showed the posted cargo pattern: no scheduled early movement needed the later time that morning, while his family's cart would leave before he returned. She accepted an earlier round after confirming the actual service interval. Yue changed the proposed row and left its old time visible in the working sheet. The young keeper smiled, relieved, then asked if the goose feeding followed the same rota. Luo said the geese refused administrative reform and would remain her household problem.

canal_p18_005.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_005.text: The downstream small-board receiver had accepted its ordinary checks only during his actual route past the house. An added evening line on the proposed rota would require another trip he had not priced. The clerk thought it only a few minutes. The receiver pointed to the longer public road he used after the outer edge remained fenced. Yue walked that route with him and counted the current interval. The extra check could move to the appointed keeper's existing return or be priced separately. It could not be shortened by a better-looking column.

canal_p18_006.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_006.text: The gardener declined a standing basin observation duty. He had once guided the field visit and wanted future notices, but his crop work needed the coming mornings. The reed gatherer offered a particular seasonal contact at his restored shelter and no permanent night turn. Luo wrote their actual answers. A trustee wanted a household representative at every low plot. The gardener asked whether the trustee planned to sleep in a bean pole. Pei laughed before catching herself. The proposed duty stayed unfilled while the bank looked for a real receiver.

canal_p18_007.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_007.text: The stall owner's nephew accepted the closure-message contact because he already bought rice before dawn. He did not accept a duty to keep other stalls informed across the whole town. The public landing receiver would carry those notices through its actual operations route. Yue wrote the two jobs separately. The nephew asked whether the contact sheet made him important enough to get better tea. His aunt said it made him responsible for reading a number correctly before ordering ingredients. He looked less pleased, then wrote the number twice in his own book.

canal_p18_008.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_008.text: Bao sat with the tilted drawing board and examined the later fastening-check row. His clinician had still restricted loaded grip. The proposed closing check would involve observation and a readable receiving diagram, with actual physical adjustment done by the separately assigned qualified worker. He could accept that lighter task only after the clinician approved it at the next review. The clerk put the acceptance pending rather than marking Bao available because he sat nearby. Bao muttered that the column now looked like his wrist felt.

canal_p18_009.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_009.text: Tian received her own letter while they worked. A sail loft downriver offered a six-week paid winter trial after a practical fitting assessment. Its start lay a fortnight after the canal closed, with priced wages and employer-provided ordinary travel under the accepted terms if she passed and chose the job. The unfinished sail order at her bench would still need delivery before departure. She read the letter twice, then tucked it away. Yue had never seen her hide good news so quickly.

canal_p18_010.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_010.text: 'Is it bad?' Yue asked after the clerk left. Tian said the offered work was good enough to make every other decision difficult. She could keep her room and steady small orders, or spend six weeks learning larger sails from people who would notice each crooked stitch. Yue said she might pass. Tian laughed. 'That is not the difficult part. I am frightened of wanting to go.' The gate seedling stood on her sill, one new leaf leaning toward the window. She looked at it as if it had somehow voted.

canal_p18_011.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_011.text: Luo offered to mind the plant during the trial if Tian chose to leave. Tian said she had not asked. Luo said she knew, then waited until Tian stopped looking at the letter. The seamstress finally asked whether the keeper truly had space away from the geese. Luo named the household window that stayed warm after the hearth was used. 'A plant can fit there,' she said. 'Your entire future would be less convenient.' Tian laughed hard enough to unfold the letter again.

canal_p18_012.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_012.text: The offered practical assessment required a small double-seam sample and an actual fitted sail corner under its intended ordinary load. Tian already had an order whose owner would permit an approved assessment after its receiving fit, if the loft agreed to observe it. She wrote that proposal through her private paid message route. Yue offered to carry the letter to the actual ordinary boat receiver while going for her own lunch. Tian accepted the small errand. Neither made it a promise to travel downriver together.

canal_p18_013.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_013.text: At the counter, a man whose daughter hoped for clerking asked why the rota named people while the trustees still spoke of households. Pei showed the charter's representation terms and the separate paid work sheet. A household could choose how to offer an opinion through its actual representative; the job named the person hired for a defined task. He wanted his daughter considered for a learning hour, not appointed to an absent adult's whole turn. Yue wrote the agreed introductory visit with Pei, who selected a time she could truly give.

canal_p18_014.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_014.text: The girl arrived carrying her row sketch and a jar of water for the inkstone, too eager to know whether either belonged in a clerk's room. Pei thanked her for the jar and asked her to read a current date from a receipt. She read the amount first. Pei turned the paper slightly and waited. The girl found the date, smiling at the correction, then asked whether keeping records always meant people argued. Pei said people argued before the records too. The girl considered that and tried the next line.

canal_p18_015.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_015.text: Han brought the future gear service receiving sheet to the rota table. His own ordinary employee would handle the specified restricted loading tasks under the private posted rates; the public receiver would check the lease's actual service and suspension terms. The bank could not appoint an unnamed worker from Han's store merely because its sheet needed a replacement column. Han offered the actual business contact and another available named shift receiver after his employee agreed. Yue saw the clerk's pen slow before writing the second name.

canal_p18_016.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_016.text: The proposed reserve keeper replacement declined because her winter care duties had changed. She did not want those private reasons put on the public board. The clerk marked the offered job unavailable and retained the actual reply in its covered schedule file. Luo arranged a fresh invitation with the real task and fixed fee. The reserve could wait under its current appointed custodian while a qualified replacement was sought; no money would be released through a convenient blank signature. Yue brought the revised invitation to the actual market board.

canal_p18_017.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_017.text: One applicant wanted the reserve job because it looked easier than hauling. Pei gave him the public task description and asked for a practical account comparison. He matched a promised private payment to the cash received column without checking its receipt. Han recognized his own earlier mistake and grinned. The applicant frowned, corrected the line after seeing the missing receipt and asked for another practice before accepting an examination date. The bank had found interest, not a finished qualification. Pei set the real second practice hour.

canal_p18_018.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_018.text: The guild trustee who had opposed the emergency allocation volunteered to receive future warning notes during his established landing visits. He had worried about reserve depletion and still did. Luo accepted the contact after comparing its actual route, then asked him to name what happened when he was away. He had an appointed public substitute already on his own standing work schedule. Yue checked that substitute's answer before writing the row. The trustee waited patiently enough that she found herself liking his careful objection more than she had at the first storm meeting.

canal_p18_019.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_019.text: At noon, a cart horse refused to pass the keeper's new rota board. Its driver insisted the white paper frightened it. Luo moved the board farther back within its ordinary viewing place, then discovered a goose sleeping directly under the cart's intended line. The goose woke indignantly and waddled away after three broom arguments. The horse passed. Tian said the paper had been innocent for once. Yue was glad somebody could laugh while the bank tried to make an entire future fit inside five straight columns.

canal_p18_020.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_020.text: The clerk caught a later copy using the old market-morning hour after the young keeper's accepted change. He replaced it before posting and told the receiver which copy was obsolete. Yue did not turn the caught copy error into another public scene about failure. The young keeper read the corrected time, then went to load his family's cart. He had a job beyond the bank's morning discussion. The rota began looking less full and more dependable as the actual people left for other things.

canal_p18_021.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_021.text: Bao's ordinary clinician accepted short light observation after the next examination found improving movement but persistent weak grip. He remained barred from loaded carpentry and would stop if pain increased. The final fastening receiving check could fit that limited role, with another qualified worker doing any physical adjustment. Bao sent the accepted restriction to the clerk. His name could now occupy a genuine later task without pretending his wrist had recovered merely because the bank wanted a familiar signature.

canal_p18_022.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_022.text: Tian asked whether Yue would come to the sail's approved fitting if the time fell before her orchard journey. Yue checked the pending appointment request and canal closing tasks before saying she could hear the actual proposed day. She would not move the overdue retained orchard duty to watch a prettier sail. Tian said she did not want that. She wanted a friend who could say yes to one known hour without promising six weeks. Yue asked for the proposed fifty-fifth afternoon after its owner agreed, and Tian wrote it into her message.

canal_p18_023.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_023.text: The gardener's daughter returned from her first clerk visit with the date practice on a spare sheet. Her father asked whether she would keep coming during sorting season. She offered one agreed learning hour after the current family work and no public job yet. He examined the row sketch she had carried into the hearing. 'You will still tell me when my count is wrong?' he asked. She said she had been doing that for years. He laughed and let her keep the spare paper dry in his better wrapper.

canal_p18_024.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_024.text: The reserve applicant completed the second practice with Pei, distinguishing actual cash, offered claim and stored equipment correctly this time. A formal qualification and appointment still needed the prescribed receiving check and trustee approval. He asked whether that meant another day of arithmetic. Pei said it meant another task he should understand before holding other people's box key. He accepted the examination time. Yue handed him the actual public reference sheet and watched him read the date before anything else.

canal_p18_025.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_025.text: By the forty-third morning, the proposed rota had several accepted duties, a genuine examination pending and a few unfilled intervals needing another arrangement. It no longer offered every household as a replacement body. Luo told the clerk to show the gaps when the trustees met instead of hiding them in a small note. The remaining keeper allowance and other fixed service terms would determine what additional tasks the bank could actually purchase. Yue carried the working sheet to the meeting, its erased times and rewritten names visible in the light.

canal_p18_026.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_026.text: The trustees asked for three final comparisons before adopting the later schedule. Luo needed the actual warning receivers and absence routes walked, Pei needed the replacement reserve applicant's practical examination supported, and Tian wanted help preparing her private sail-loft sample without delaying the owner's current order. The public duties would proceed under their receivers; the private sample had its own promised hour. Yue could stand beside the bank's future call, its box of money or a friend whose winter might now happen somewhere else.

canal_p18_027.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_027.text: Tian put the sample cloth beside the completed customer seams, looking suddenly less sure than she had when defending a household at the hearing. Bao offered his tilted board as a light measuring surface if she wanted it, then kept his supported hand away from the scissors. Luo took the warning sheets outside to find the real distant voice positions. Pei set a receipt and an unpowered tile on her table for different sorts of count. Yue chose where to give the afternoon's attention before the forty-fourth-day adoption.

canal_p18_028.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_028.text: Yue watched Tian measure the sample's grain twice before touching the scissors. The seamstress caught her staring. 'You are relieved it is my examination,' she said. Yue admitted that she was. Tian handed her a plain corner of offcut and asked her to mark a straight allowance. Yue's first line wandered near its end. Tian laughed, took the ruler back and showed her how the cloth shifted under a careless thumb. The public apprentice had found a small private subject in which her cord was completely useless.

canal_p18_029.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_029.text: The clerk left the later rota unposted until its final receivers were checked. Yue could walk the warning handover with Luo, support the reserve applicant's practical account examination or help Tian prepare the approved sail-loft sample. The public gaps would not disappear whichever task she chose. Tian's possible winter work would not make her father's old pledge return. The afternoon held both a common future and a private one, and they could grow beside the same canal without asking to become each other's property.

choices.text: Walk the warning receivers with Luo Zhen.
Help Tian Min prepare the sail sample.

canal_p18_030.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_030.text: Luo led the warning walk before sunrise, when the towpath smelled of cold mud and the bakery had only begun its fire. Her lamp made the painted marks appear farther apart than they were. Yue carried the new receiver list inside her coat. At the first cottage a man opened his window and immediately asked whether the gate had failed. Luo lowered the lamp. "The gate is sleeping. We are the fools awake." His wife called from the bed that this was the first sensible warning the keeper had ever delivered.

canal_p18_031.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_031.text: They waited while the man put on both shoes, rather than accepting his promise to listen from the kitchen. The changed path turned behind a stacked woodpile; there the bell lost its clear edge. Luo had walked it in daylight and disliked discovering that sound could have a corner. The man tapped the new mark with his heel. "I can hear a cart here. I cannot hear whether you want me to stay or go." Yue asked him to repeat what he actually heard. He produced three beautiful, completely useless syllables.

canal_p18_032.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_032.text: The second receiver had already left for the early vegetable boat. His mother sat beside the stove, cutting spoiled leaves from cabbages. She offered to take his place, then admitted she could not manage the outer footbridge in darkness. Luo put the spare message back into her sleeve. They agreed on the nearer covered doorway, reached without that bridge, and tried the spoken relay there. The woman heard it cleanly. Her laugh when she answered was louder than either warning. "My son can go sell cabbages. I have finally received an office."

canal_p18_033.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_033.text: A dog followed them from the covered doorway, carrying a strip of straw as if it too had been appointed. At the raised turn it tried to pass between Luo's feet. Yue caught her elbow before the keeper stepped onto the loose edge, then let go when she had her balance. No bell or qi could make the wet strip wider. Luo swore at the dog and at the carpenter who had left the corner unmarked. The dog abandoned its straw, which seemed to be a resignation from public service.

canal_p18_034.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_034.text: Beyond the turn they found the gardener measuring her damaged bed with a string. She had heard their voices and come out thinking someone wanted a decision about the channel. Luo explained the exercise. The woman leaned on her spade. "If you put me on that list, I will come running every time. I will lose the beans that survived while I save the ones that drowned." She wanted a warning at her own door, not a duty to inspect everyone's plots. Yue crossed out the copied household heading and kept the actual receiver.

canal_p18_035.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_035.text: The gardener lent them a dry board to stand on while they tested the lower call. She stayed inside and answered through the shutters. That distance was useful; her generosity did not qualify the garden as a future warning station. Luo moved the mark back toward the public turn, where a receiver could reach it without trampling beds. The keeper looked annoyed at losing the shorter route. "My feet have been cheating this canal for twenty years." The gardener answered that she would send a bill to the feet separately.

canal_p18_036.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_036.text: At the last cottage a child repeated the withdrawal instruction flawlessly, then added that everyone should bring three steamed buns. The adult receiver was embarrassed. Yue asked where the buns came from. Last year's ferry warning, the child explained, because an uncle had waited hungry at the landing. Luo sat on the doorstep and disentangled the two events with him. He knew which route was for the gate and which for the ferry; he simply preferred the one with food. The adult practiced the exact call again, without revising the child's appetite.

canal_p18_037.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_037.text: By full light the walk had acquired two changed positions, one alternate receiver, and a corner requiring a visible edge before anyone used it at night. Luo drew these on the board herself. Her handwriting resembled lengths of rope dropped from a height. Yue offered to copy it. "You may make it legible," Luo said, "but keep the ugly turn ugly. When I draw a straight line through that place, someone younger will believe me." She rubbed a thumb across the damp charcoal and drew the bend a second time.

canal_p18_038.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_038.text: They returned by the bakery and bought a single warm loaf from their own purses, dividing it on the doorstep. Luo gave the dog no bread, then dropped a heel apparently by accident. She spoke of the young keeper's market work without complaint for the first time. If the girl earned enough from her stall, she could afford to remain nearby; a perfect rota that drove her away would leave Luo carrying the keys again. Yue asked whether she had told the girl this. Luo stared at the loaf as if it had betrayed her.

canal_p18_039.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_039.text: The morning report contained the failed corner call and the changed doorway, rather than a statement that every household was covered. The repair clerk priced marking the loose edge within the remaining path task. Luo took the receiver corrections to the young keeper herself. Their conversation happened behind the gate shed; Yue heard one sharp reply, a pause, and then laughter at a remark she could not make out. When Luo emerged, she gave Yue the clean copy. There were still gaps in winter service, but one difficult conversation had actually occurred.

canal_p18_040.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_040.text: Pei Fen put three sample purses on the examination table and told the reserve applicant that none contained the money he hoped to be paid. He blinked at her. "Then why purses?" "Because you were much less confused yesterday when I said bag." The girl who had come for a learning hour hid a smile in her sleeve. Yue sat beside the door, where she could witness answers without feeding them to him. Outside, someone was sharpening a scythe with strokes that sounded far more confident than the young man's breathing.

canal_p18_041.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_041.text: The first sample account concerned an ordinary keeper round interrupted by a closed footbridge. The applicant initially wrote a full repair day against the monthly service fee, then stopped himself. He looked at the brief appointment sheet and asked what work had actually been requested. Pei nodded for him to continue. He proposed completing the safe nearer round and reporting the missed reach. Yue had wanted to help when he hesitated; she kept her hands still. His correction mattered more than the speed with which her finger could have found the right line.

canal_p18_042.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_042.text: For the second problem Pei produced a private carpenter's tool wrapped in cloth. The applicant reached toward it, assuming that anything laid on an official table belonged to the canal. Bao, seated at the window for a brief permitted observation, said, "That plane has fed my sister's family. Ask the table whose it is." The applicant withdrew his hand and requested permission before examining the damaged blade. Bao granted it. He had brought an old, blunt tool for the exercise, but his annoyance at the assumption was entirely fresh.

canal_p18_043.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_043.text: The last problem was a missing receipt, not missing coin. Pei's small handwriting had become difficult for her to inspect under the cloudy light, so she asked the applicant to read the dates aloud. He found a delivery acknowledgment on the wrong side of the folder and wanted to repair the account immediately. Yue asked what the supplier would see on returning. He reconsidered and placed a dated correction beside the original. Pei let him finish without praise. The girl recorded each step, her tongue pressed against her lip in concentration.

canal_p18_044.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_044.text: A sudden gust pushed rain through the upper window. The applicant scrambled to rescue all three purses and left the actual papers exposed. Pei slapped a dry cover over them. The girl shut the window. Bao laughed once, then winced when his supported wrist shifted against the chair. The applicant looked miserably at his dripping sleeve. "The purses have survived." "Excellent," Pei said. "They were worth almost nothing." Yue fetched a cloth from the kitchen and gave it to him without turning his mistake into a permanent verdict on his character.

canal_p18_045.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_045.text: When the table was dry, Pei repeated the interrupted problem. This time he protected the account first, then moved the tool and bags with the owner's agreement. He did not try to hide the earlier error in his notes. The examination concerned reserve record work and receiver practice, not permission to operate powered equipment or climb the gate. Its result could recommend a limited appointment; the trustees still had to accept the actual hours and fee. He listened to this with relief. The small job had become difficult enough without an imaginary larger one.

canal_p18_046.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_046.text: At midday the girl left to carry lunch to her father. She asked Pei whether she might return next week. Pei nearly said yes before remembering how many promises could fit inside that small word. They chose one more learning hour after the girl's household work, with no claim of wages or future employment. At the door the girl said she liked the accounts better when they contained arguments. "Then you have chosen an inexhaustible subject," Pei replied. Yue saw the clerk's shoulders straighten as the child ran down the steps.

canal_p18_047.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_047.text: The trustees' representative arrived with the current service sheet, not a purse of extra money. He accepted the reserve applicant for two supervised receiver rounds within the existing fee and named the principal keeper who would check them. Any later extension would need its own appointment. The young man read the terms twice, then signed. His first task was to carry the corrected warning list to the nearer cottages. He asked whether he could leave the sample purses behind. Pei waved him away before her laughter spoiled the dignity of the examination.

canal_p18_048.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_048.text: After everyone had gone, Pei turned the three purses inside out to dry. Yue asked whether she wanted a younger clerk assigned for winter. "Assigned to what?" Pei replied. "To my chair, my mistakes, or my reputation?" She rubbed her tired eyes, then admitted she wanted someone who could read tiny dates before supper without guessing. They wrote that concrete need into the next invitation. Yue did not offer to remain indefinitely. Her canal term had an end; Pei's work needed an answer that would still exist after Yue had walked away.

canal_p18_049.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_049.text: The examination report preserved the wrong first entry, the corrected answer, and the interrupted exercise. Bao's contribution was a short statement about his private plane, paid only within the light observation interval already approved for him. He left before stiffness made the clinic's warning necessary again. Pei watched him go and put a broad mark beside the accepted record tasks. "A person can be useful before becoming useful at everything," she said. Yue recognized the remark as partly meant for her. This time she allowed it to pass without an argument.

canal_p18_050.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_050.text: Tian cleared a space in the loft above the sail seller's stall. The roof was so low that Yue struck a beam on arriving and then thanked it politely, which made Tian laugh until she dropped her chalk. An approved scrap of sailcloth lay across two trestles; the owner had agreed to the small sample and the intended test load. It was not the actual customer's sail. Tian showed Yue the doubled seam, then pointed to the place where her last stitch had pulled crooked. "That," she said, "is what I keep seeing when I try to sleep."

canal_p18_051.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_051.text: Yue studied the seam and could find no fault until Tian turned it over. A tiny gathered fold made the corner climb away from the table. Yue offered to hold the cloth flat. Tian placed her hands, then moved them farther apart. "You hold things as though they have promised to fight you." "Most of them do." "This one is only trying to become a sail." They worked in silence for several minutes. The cloth relaxed under a steadier grip. Yue's cultivation did nothing useful for learning where Tian needed an ordinary thumb.

canal_p18_052.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_052.text: The observer from the sail seller inspected the test arrangement before they placed the small rated weights. Yue had imagined a dramatic snap proving Tian's work; the actual trial involved watching a seam under steady tension while the observer counted. A loose corner lifted gradually. Tian saw it before the count ended and asked to stop. The weights came off in reverse order. She pressed her knuckles to her forehead. Yue started to reassure her, then noticed Tian looking not for comfort but for the exact point of movement on the cloth.

canal_p18_053.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_053.text: They marked the lifted corner in chalk and unpicked only the short faulty run. Tian spoke while her knife slid beneath the thread. Her mother thought a six-week trial was a polite way for a distant employer to obtain cheap winter work. Tian herself feared that passing would make departure real. Neither worry could be answered by praising the repaired seam. Yue asked what the written offer said about lodging and ordinary return travel. Tian fetched it from a dry tube. The terms were plain enough to examine and still left the choice of leaving painfully hers.

canal_p18_054.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_054.text: The sail seller's observer went downstairs to meet a buyer, leaving the sample unloaded. Tian asked whether Yue had ever wanted to remain somewhere merely because she had finally become good at being there. Yue thought of familiar training walls, the people who knew her old failures, and roads that began with another person's emergency. "Often," she said. "I am still bad at knowing when that wish deserves obedience." Tian held up the loose thread. "I hoped for a wiser answer." "Then you should have invited the roof beam. It stopped me immediately."

canal_p18_055.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_055.text: Tian's mother arrived carrying pickled radish and a formidable expression. She had come to feed them; she also wanted to see the offer. Yue ate beside the window while mother and daughter read the same line differently three times. At last the mother asked who would look after Tian if she fell ill downriver. The written lodging terms named a resident forewoman, whom Tian had already asked about. It was an answer with a person behind it. Her mother still disliked the distance, but the argument moved beyond a road imagined as endless darkness.

canal_p18_056.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_056.text: The observer returned for the second sample trial. Tian had widened the doubled run by a measured amount and checked the new stitch tension before loading. This time the corner held through the full observation interval. The result qualified this sample, not the unseen customer's sail or Tian's entire winter employment. The observer wrote what had actually been tested and promised to send it with the appointment request. Tian took the paper without grinning until he went downstairs. Then she pressed both palms flat on the trestle and whispered, "I did want this."

canal_p18_057.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_057.text: They carried the scrap outside to examine it in daylight. Wind filled the loose cloth for an instant and pulled Yue's hand toward the rail. She moved her feet instead of resisting with her arm, and Tian seized the nearest corner. The sample settled against their coats like a stubborn bird. No one had been in danger, but they both laughed harder than the small incident deserved. Below them, Tian's mother shouted that if they were testing flight she refused the trial entirely. Tian called back that the sail had already failed to transport its crew.

canal_p18_058.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_058.text: The afternoon's private sample hours came from Tian's own preparation and the seller's agreed observation, rather than the canal repair account. Yue's help fit the previously named short interval; she still had the later public tasks she had accepted. Before leaving she helped Tian lay the finished scrap in a dry wrapper. Tian wanted to give it to her as a keepsake. Yue declined the bulky cloth gently and asked for one small thread instead. Tian cut it from the waste edge. It would remind her of a friend's work without carrying someone else's test record into another journey.

canal_p18_059.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_059.text: When they brought the report to Pei, Tian read the exact result aloud herself. The clerk asked about the proposed Day Fifty-Five fitting and noted that the customer and loft still had to confirm it. Tian no longer treated that unanswered request as a verdict. She took a copy home to discuss the practical travel terms with her mother. Yue watched her cross the landing with the tube tucked inside her coat. The town had offered Tian a thousand ways to be needed. For the first time she carried an equally concrete possibility of going elsewhere.

canal_p18_060.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_060.text: On the evening of the forty-third day, the three task reports lay beside the rota. They did not agree on everything, which made Luo trust them more. The warning walk had changed a receiving position; the reserve examination had limited the new appointment; the sail sample had earned a result without settling Tian's future. Yue read the corrections while a moth battered the lamp shade. At the bottom Pei left a blank space for the two winter gaps. Someone offered to fill it with household names. The clerk covered the space with her hand.

canal_p18_061.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_061.text: The young keeper arrived late from market with bruised pears she had bought cheaply for herself. She put two beside Luo and kept the better one. Luo accepted her share without commenting on the hierarchy. They agreed on the earlier morning round and the exact route the girl could finish before opening her stall. If ice closed the farther walk, its service would be reported as interrupted, not silently shifted to an unpaid neighbor. The girl asked whether this meant she could now sleep on market nights. Luo said the pears had bought considerable goodwill.

canal_p18_062.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_062.text: The fixed monthly keeper fee of four copper covered the short agreed rounds and their accepted division. It did not create a purse for repairs, overnight watching, or an extra clerk. Pei placed those different tasks on different lines. The reserve applicant's supervised receiver practice fitted the same service appointment; he would not be paid twice for the same round. When he saw the sheet, he asked what happened if the principal keeper was ill. Luo replied that illness required an actual substitute and a changed arrangement. "You may not solve it by becoming two people."

canal_p18_063.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_063.text: One winter gap was the outer path after the late grain boat. The receiving mark there could be reached safely in daylight, but no one had accepted an unpriced night journey. The trustees decided to suspend that late use in weather requiring the gate warning unless a paid receiver was appointed. The boat owner disliked the restriction and wrote it down anyway. Yue saw the real cost enter his face: fewer convenient trips, possible custom lost. The restriction would have been easier to praise had it fallen upon a person who was not in the room.

canal_p18_064.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_064.text: The other gap concerned record checking when Pei's eyes tired. The trustees approved a small invitation defining two short weekly intervals within the remaining administrative allocation for the closing week. A winter continuation would require a separately funded appointment. The farmer's daughter was not entered simply because she enjoyed her lesson. Pei protested that the announcement made her sound ancient. The girl, passing the door with an empty lunch bowl, said nobody ancient would argue so loudly. Pei threw a clean paper ball at her and missed by a splendid distance.

canal_p18_065.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_065.text: By morning the rejected household headings had become useful scratch paper. Tian cut one sheet into labels for her samples and kept the unused addresses out of the public waste basket. The neat columns had looked authoritative yesterday; now they held measurements and grocery lists. Yue found this satisfying until a trustee asked why the official copy was late. Corrections took time that the old careless sheet had seemed to save. She carried the actual approved rota to him instead of defending the delay in the abstract. He checked it, signed, and asked for his own receiving hour.

canal_p18_066.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_066.text: Bao came to the gate for a brief light observation on the forty-fourth day. He wore the wrist support under his sleeve and pretended the chair had been placed for someone older. Luo left it directly behind him until he surrendered. His uninjured hand could trace a line on the drawing; the injured one still failed when he tried to close it firmly. Yue moved the heavy rule within reach of the worker who would measure the frame. Bao stared at the transferred task, then looked away toward the canal. The loss was smaller than his pride and more stubborn.

canal_p18_067.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_067.text: The repair clerk proposed transferring a quarter-day equivalent of Bao's unstarted closing carpentry to the qualified mason who had already inspected the outlet. The mason accepted the physical adjustment at the same ordinary two-copper daily rate. Bao retained his agreed light observation and the work he had actually completed. This changed assignments inside the existing twenty-eight equivalents; it added neither a hidden workday nor an unpaid helper. Bao asked for the revised line before agreeing. When he saw it, he said, "At least my bad wrist is not being used as a cheap door hinge."

canal_p18_068.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_068.text: The revised ordinary allocations now left Bao four and a quarter equivalents and the mason one and three quarters, with the other accepted shares unchanged. These were totals of paid hours, not a demand to work straight days through meals and injuries. Pei kept the earlier transfers beside the new one so a closing reader could follow them. Yue checked her own twelve equivalents against the hours still outstanding. She had not earned the final portion merely by remaining in town. The last inspections and report work had to happen before her twenty-four copper became wholly due.

canal_p18_069.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_069.text: At the little house beside the spill, the grandmother had hung her recovered cup from a peg rather than leaving it on the shelf. It knocked against the wall whenever the door opened. Yue asked whether that bothered her. "It tells me the house is still moving," she said. Her daughter wanted to plant winter greens where the soaked herbs had been. They argued about the shade, not the evacuation. Luo waited on the step until invited inside, bringing the corrected warning position and no new claim on their time. The grandmother made tea strong enough to bend a spoon.

canal_p18_070.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_070.text: The gardener received the rota at her door and found her name only where she had agreed to hear a warning. She asked about the unresolved crop loss. The claims clerk's reply remained the same: recorded, supported where possible, not wholly paid by the private ten-copper fund. Yue hated saying it after accepting the woman's tea, yet a warmer answer would have spent money that did not exist. The gardener turned the page over and wrote next spring's seed list. "Then stop admiring my patience," she said. "Help me price what I have to try again."

canal_p18_071.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_071.text: They spent a short personal interval comparing seed sellers' offers. Yue did not choose a crop for a field she would not tend. The gardener rejected the cheapest packet because she knew how poorly it stored in her damp shed. She chose a smaller quantity from a seller who would divide the sack at the quoted rate. Her four copper from the independent hardship fund covered part of the plan; the rest required her own sale of stored beans. She kept the food grain separate. Feeding the household and planting the spring were two arguments on the same kitchen table.

canal_p18_072.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_072.text: At the reed shelter the cutter had repaired his spoon handle with a brass binding from his own scrap box. His wife was sorting the partly saved reeds for roof, mat, and fuel. Yue reached for a wet bundle and was told sharply to leave it; mixed bundles would spoil the last good stock. She stepped back. The cutter handed her a dry one instead. Their rebuilt roof had not restored the old pile or its labor. Under it, however, they could disagree about work without standing in rain. The small difference made the shelter feel occupied again.

canal_p18_073.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_073.text: Han opened the returned private store chest while the former receiver watched its security mark being removed. Only listed property was released; the carpenters' tools had never belonged under that claim. Inside were folded tarpaulins, two cracked bowls, and a mouse's elaborate winter plan. Han looked at the ruined nesting straw for a long time. "Even the mouse thought this place had a future." Tian, who had come to confirm a private sewing bill already paid from the emergency materials line, said the mouse had at least worked without sending notices to anyone's grandchildren.

canal_p18_074.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_074.text: The damp family letters were still with the private conservator Han had chosen and paid. Their unfinished drying was not used as a reason to hold the public account open. Han asked Yue whether she wanted to see the pieces when they returned. She said yes, if he still wished it then. His wife sat beside the chest and sorted the cracked bowls rather than answering for him. Yue recognized the restraint as a harder kindness than her immediate curiosity. The letters would belong to a living conversation, not become evidence merely because the town now trusted him less blindly.

canal_p18_075.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_075.text: The remaining repair list concerned the outer return path, the displaced edge mark, and the dry receiving condition of the small apparatus. A new powered trial was not authorized. Jiang's funded appointments had ended, and the road crew had gone back to their ordinary contracts. The commission could inspect the stored frame and the accepted earlier results without pretending absent operators were free. Luo was relieved to hear this and then annoyed at herself for being relieved. She had begun to associate every test with the possibility of another night without sleep.

canal_p18_076.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_076.text: Pei sent the revised invitation and path restriction with the regular paid office dispatch. Yue's separate orchard request still awaited Matron Ren's actual acceptance. The clinic and patients needed the review interval she had described; an unanswered proposal had not become an appointment merely because Yue wrote it neatly. She folded the latest copied inquiry into her personal papers. Tian noticed the gesture and asked whether waiting ever became easier. "Sometimes the thing arrives," Yue replied. "That is the closest I have found." Tian accepted this answer with considerably less irritation than the earlier one.

canal_p18_077.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_077.text: Rain returned in short, ordinary showers. People hurried washing under roofs and moved food baskets off the steps, but no one called every dark cloud an emergency. The young keeper completed her accepted morning round and opened her stall on time. The reserve receiver made one supervised journey, forgot a doorway, returned, and corrected his list. Bao went home before his wrist stiffened. Yue watched these imperfect completions from the landing and felt the town moving past the appetite to solve everything in a single glorious day. Its pace still left plenty for tomorrow.

canal_p18_078.speaker: narrator
canal_p18_078.text: At dusk the mason laid out the approved hand tools for the return-path work. The rough stones would come from usable material already in the commission store, selected and accounted for without a new purchase. Luo showed him the loose turn on her ugly drawing. Bao sat beside them for his short final look and pointed with his sound hand. The canal shone between two wet banks, carrying the last light farther than anyone could walk. Yue put away the rota. Tomorrow they would repair the place their tidy lines had repeatedly tried to step across.
